platform_transparency.free_introductory_usage: Framer offers introductory capabilities and free subdomain publishing (.framer.app), subject to current platform terms.
platform_transparency.custom_domains: Connecting a third-party custom domain requires an eligible paid Framer Site plan.
platform_transparency.cms_limitations: CMS collection counts, item limits, and publishing permissions depend on the active plan tier.
platform_transparency.ai_features: AI generation features, credits, and usage quotas may vary and are subject to platform terms.
platform_transparency.cost_transparency: Commercial client projects may involve site hosting subscriptions, custom domain fees, premium typography licenses, and optional third-party integrations.

why_now.industry_shift: Modern tech startups, creative agencies, and top design studios increasingly adopt Framer to publish interactive, visually stunning websites without engineering bottlenecks.
why_now.ai_impact: AI tools accelerate layout wireframing, but mastering responsive stacks, motion choreography, and CMS content architecture requires essential human design expertise.
why_now.business_demand: Brands demand dynamic marketing pages and portfolio experiences that load rapidly, adapt flawlessly across mobile, and engage visitors through subtle motion.
why_now.career_opportunity: Designers who build and publish live Framer websites command premium freelance rates and lead high-impact marketing design projects.

target_audience.not_designed_for: Developers looking for complex transactional e-commerce, custom shopping carts, backend API development, full-stack React application engineering, or enterprise database administration.

prerequisites.not_required: Advanced coding (JavaScript/React) or mandatory prior Figma expertise.
prerequisites.hardware_software: Computer with high-speed internet and modern web browser capable of running Framer smoothly; free Framer account.

Backend server application development and custom database engineering
Full-stack React application development or custom React code components

modules.module_purpose: Understand Framer's design and publishing workflow while applying essential visual design principles.

lessons.what_is_taught: What Framer is, design-to-web workflow, suitable website use cases (landing pages, marketing sites, portfolios), visual development fundamentals, Framer account and project setup, and overview of platform plans and limits.
subtopics: Understanding the Framer ecosystem and browser-based visual canvas

Framer workspace setup, project management, and dashboard navigation

lessons.what_is_taught: Framer canvas navigation, layers panel, pages panel, properties panel, assets library, preview mode, project settings, and publishing overview.

The Layers panel: managing frames, hierarchy, and naming conventions
The Pages panel: organizing static pages, CMS collection templates, and redirects
The Properties panel: dimensions, layout, styling, effects, and code overrides
The Assets library: color styles, text styles, graphics, and components
Previewing designs in desktop/mobile simulation and staging publishing
lessons.what_learner_does: Navigates all Framer interface panels, configures project settings, and publishes a staging test.
lessons.why_it_matters: Fluency in Framer's UI dramatically accelerates visual web creation and iteration.

Audience persona identification and visitor journey mapping
Defining measurable website objectives (leads, inquiries, case study views)
Constructing an organized visual sitemap with logical page relationships
Content hierarchy: structuring above-the-fold value propositions and supporting proof
Navigation planning: primary menu, mobile drawer, and footer links
lessons.what_learner_does: Drafts a commercial website brief, visual sitemap, and content hierarchy outline.
lessons.why_it_matters: Thorough planning prevents structural rework and produces conversion-focused marketing sites.
lessons.expected_outcome: Approved sitemap and content blueprint for the multi-page website.

subtopics: Typography fundamentals: font pairing, modular scales, line heights, and letter spacing
Color theory: brand primary, dark neutral text, light backgrounds, and functional accents
Color contrast ratios for legibility and WCAG AA compliance
Establishing visual hierarchy to guide visitor attention naturally
Alignment principles: grid alignment, edge alignment, and visual balance
The intentional use of white space to create a premium, uncluttered aesthetic
lessons.what_learner_does: Creates visual moodboards and applies typography scales and color harmony to page wireframes.
lessons.why_it_matters: High visual craft is what elevates modern Framer websites into award-winning digital experiences.
lessons.expected_outcome: Visual design foundation with established typography scales and color harmony.

lessons.what_is_taught: Creating reusable style systems in Framer: global text styles (H1-H6, Body, Caption), color styles (tokens), spacing conventions (8pt grid), brand application, and asset preparation.
subtopics: Defining global Text Styles in Framer's Assets panel
Creating shared Color Styles (tokens) for backgrounds, surfaces, and text
Implementing an 8pt spatial layout scale for consistent padding and margins
Applying brand assets: vector SVG logos, icons, and photography guidelines
Maintaining design token governance across multi-page projects
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a centralized style system in Framer with linked text and color tokens.
lessons.why_it_matters: Centralized styles allow instant brand updates and guarantee visual uniformity.
lessons.expected_outcome: Comprehensive Framer style system with global text and color styles.

lessons.what_is_taught: Figma reference preparation, understanding Auto Layout translation, design conversion, available import/copy workflows (HTML-to-Framer plugin / copy-paste), asset transfer, and manual cleanup after import.
subtopics: Preparing Figma frames with Auto Layout for clean translation
Using official Figma to Framer copy/import workflows
Translating Figma Auto Layout properties into Framer Stacks
Exporting optimized image assets (SVG, WebP) from Figma
Executing manual cleanup: fixing layout direction, constraints, and font bindings

subtopics: Leveraging Framer AI prompts for initial page wireframe ideation
Generating preliminary draft copy and placeholder section structures
Exploring alternative design themes and palette variations
Auditing AI output for visual consistency, typography issues, and layout flaws
The human designer's role: manual refinement, curation, and critical judgment
lessons.what_learner_does: Generates an initial section wireframe with AI assistance, then manually refines typography and spacing.
lessons.why_it_matters: AI accelerates drafting, but professional client delivery demands human taste and precision.
lessons.expected_outcome: Refined, human-approved layout crafted with initial AI ideation.

modules.hands_on_practice: Build the visual foundation of a startup, agency or portfolio website.

modules.module_purpose: Create responsive, adaptable website layouts using Framer's native layout systems.

lessons.what_is_taught: Framer frames vs div containers, nested frame hierarchy, content containment, layer organization, positioning concepts (relative vs absolute), and layout nesting.
subtopics: The Frame element: the atomic building block of Framer layouts
Nested frame hierarchy and logical DOM structure
Frame clipping and content containment properties
Relative vs absolute positioning: why modern layouts avoid absolute positioning
Layer naming hygiene and grouping conventions for maintainability
lessons.what_learner_does: Constructs clean frame hierarchies and structures nested containers for page sections.
lessons.why_it_matters: Proper frame containment prevents layout breaking and simplifies responsive adaptation.
lessons.expected_outcome: Structured, clean frame architecture across page sections.

lessons.what_is_taught: Framer Stacks (Flexbox equivalent): vertical stacks, horizontal stacks, layout direction, alignment, distribution, gap properties, padding, and nested stacks.
subtopics: Understanding Stacks: Framer's visual implementation of modern Flexbox
Direction controls: Row (horizontal) vs Column (vertical) stacks
Alignment properties: Start, Center, End, Stretch
Distribution controls: Start, Center, End, Space Between, Space Around
Managing Gap properties for uniform child spacing without margin hacks
Building complex responsive sections using nested horizontal and vertical stacks
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds navigation headers, feature blocks, and testimonial rows using nested stacks.
lessons.why_it_matters: Stacks are the foundation of fluid, responsive, code-standard layouts in Framer.
lessons.expected_outcome: Mastery of Framer horizontal and vertical stack layout manipulation.

lessons.what_is_taught: Framer Grid structures: columns, rows, responsive grid behavior, portfolio grids, service matrices, card collections, and auto-fitting grid items.
subtopics: Configuring Framer Grid elements for two-dimensional layouts
Defining column and row templates and track proportions
Managing grid gaps and item alignment within grid cells
Building responsive portfolio galleries and service card matrices
Auto-fitting grid behavior across shrinking viewports
lessons.what_learner_does: Designs a multi-card portfolio gallery and features matrix using Framer Grids.
lessons.why_it_matters: Grids allow structured, two-dimensional card layouts that reconfigure cleanly.
lessons.expected_outcome: Production-ready portfolio and feature grid layouts.

lessons.what_is_taught: Framer sizing models: Fixed sizing (px), Relative sizing (%), Fill (flex-grow), Fit Content (hug content), Min/Max width and height constraints, and overflow handling (visible, hidden, scroll).
subtopics: Mastering Fixed vs Relative (%) sizing in Framer
The Fill property: expanding child elements to occupy available container space
The Fit Content property: shrinking containers to hug internal elements snugly
Setting Minimum and Maximum width/height constraints for large screens
Managing overflow behavior: preventing unwanted horizontal scrolling
lessons.what_learner_does: Configures Fill and Fit Content properties to achieve fluid, dynamic container behavior.
lessons.why_it_matters: Understanding sizing behavior prevents rigid, brittle layouts that break on different monitors.
lessons.expected_outcome: Fluid layout sizing adapting naturally without clipping or unwanted overflow.

lessons.what_is_taught: Framer responsive breakpoints: Desktop (1200px+), Tablet (810px), Mobile (390px), breakpoint cascade rules, breakpoint-specific styling, responsive typography, and content stacking.
subtopics: The Framer breakpoint cascade: changes flow from primary Desktop down to Mobile
Adding and adjusting Tablet and Mobile breakpoint viewports
Overriding layout direction on Mobile (changing horizontal rows to vertical stacks)
Responsive typography: adjusting heading sizes and line heights per breakpoint
Adaptive image scaling and responsive container width adjustments
lessons.what_learner_does: Adapts page layouts across Desktop, Tablet, and Mobile breakpoints using cascade overrides.
lessons.why_it_matters: Over 60% of web visits occur on mobile devices; flawless responsive execution is essential.
lessons.expected_outcome: Seamless responsive adaptation across desktop, tablet, and mobile breakpoints.

lessons.what_is_taught: Designing reusable section layouts: responsive navigation components, buttons, feature cards, footers, and section variants.
subtopics: Building a responsive navigation bar that switches to a mobile drawer menu
Creating responsive card layouts with adaptive padding and image heights
Standardizing button sizes and touch targets across breakpoints
Structuring multi-column footer layouts that collapse cleanly on mobile
Configuring section variants for alternate visual rhythms
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a modular set of responsive layout sections ready for page assembly.
lessons.why_it_matters: Modular responsive sections ensure consistent spacing and rapid page construction.
lessons.expected_outcome: Suite of reusable responsive layout components.

lessons.what_is_taught: Mobile-first quality standards: touch target sizing (48px+), typography legibility on handheld screens, spacing scales, image cropping behavior, mobile navigation usability, and eliminating horizontal overflow.
subtopics: Ensuring accessible 48px+ touch targets for interactive mobile elements
Verifying mobile text legibility and preventing awkward word breaks
Adjusting padding and margins to maximize mobile screen real estate
Controlling image focal points and aspect ratios on narrow viewports
Testing mobile hamburger drawer transitions and dismiss triggers
Hunting and eliminating horizontal overflow (the dreaded mobile side-scroll)
lessons.what_learner_does: Performs a rigorous mobile audit and eliminates all touch-target and overflow issues.
lessons.why_it_matters: Mobile quality directly impacts bounce rates, user satisfaction, and search rankings.
lessons.expected_outcome: Polished, ergonomic mobile user experience across all sections.

lessons.what_is_taught: Framer layout debugging: fixing broken alignment, resolving overflowing elements, correcting unexpected sizing behavior, troubleshooting inconsistent spacing, resolving breakpoint conflicts, and systematic responsive QA.
subtopics: Diagnosing common Framer layout bugs: runaway Fill containers and clipped text
Resolving alignment conflicts inside nested stacks
Resetting accidental breakpoint property overrides
Verifying min/max constraints against extreme screen resolutions
Systematic cross-device QA checklist execution
lessons.what_learner_does: Audits a complex multi-section layout, diagnoses layout errors, and applies fixes.
lessons.why_it_matters: Systematic layout debugging separates professional web creators from novices.
lessons.expected_outcome: Bug-free, responsive layout system verified across all viewports.

modules.module_purpose: Build reusable interactive components and meaningful motion experiences without compromising accessibility or performance.

lessons.what_is_taught: Framer component fundamentals: creating components from layers, component instances, component organization in the Assets panel, and propagating updates across the project.
subtopics: Creating Framer Components from selected frames and stacks
Understanding the relationship between master components and instances
Organizing components in the Assets panel with logical folder naming
Component property controls: exposing text overrides, image swaps, and link targets
Editing master components and verifying global updates across all pages
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a modular component library with exposed properties for text and media.
lessons.why_it_matters: Components allow rapid site building and ensure single-source-of-truth maintainability.
lessons.expected_outcome: Organized Framer component library with exposed customization properties.

lessons.what_is_taught: Component variants in Framer: visual states (Default, Hover, Pressed, Active), interactive button variants, size variants (Small, Medium, Large), and state transitions.
subtopics: Creating component variants for different visual and functional states
Configuring Default, Hover, and Pressed states for interactive elements
Creating size and theme variants (e.g. Primary, Secondary, Outline)
Configuring smooth spring or ease transitions between variants
Testing variant state switches directly on the canvas
lessons.what_learner_does: Designs interactive buttons and cards with Hover and Pressed variants.
lessons.why_it_matters: Variants provide tactile visual feedback that makes interfaces feel responsive and alive.
lessons.expected_outcome: Interactive component suite with smooth variant transitions.

lessons.what_is_taught: Building interactive components: dropdown navigation menus, mobile drawer overlays, interactive hover cards, CTA button states, accordions, and state-based feedback.
subtopics: Constructing an interactive accordion component with open/closed variants
Building a desktop dropdown menu with hover-activated sub-navigation
Creating a mobile full-screen drawer menu with animated entrance/exit
Interactive card components with image zoom and elevation changes on hover
Providing clear visual feedback for all interactive states
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds an accessible interactive FAQ accordion and mobile navigation drawer.
lessons.why_it_matters: Interactive components condense complex information into engaging user interfaces.
lessons.expected_outcome: Functioning interactive accordion and navigation components.

lessons.what_is_taught: Motion design principles for the web: timing, duration (150ms-400ms), easing curves (spring physics vs cubic bezier), visual feedback, motion hierarchy, and purposeful animation.
subtopics: The role of motion in modern digital product design
Understanding Framer's spring physics: damping, stiffness, and mass
Standard transition durations for micro-interactions vs page transitions
Establishing motion hierarchy: guiding the user's focus purposefully
Avoiding gratuitous animation: knowing when stillness is superior
lessons.what_learner_does: Calibrates spring physics and transition curves to achieve natural, refined motion.
lessons.why_it_matters: Polished motion design communicates premium brand craft without distracting users.
lessons.expected_outcome: Refined spring physics and easing presets applied across interactive elements.

lessons.what_is_taught: Hover interactions, scroll-triggered appear effects, entrance animations, opacity fades, transform animations (translate, scale), and subtle content emphasis.
subtopics: Configuring Framer Appear animations: Scroll In View vs Mount triggers
Staggered entrance effects for grid cards and headline text
Smooth micro-scaling and elevation shadows on card hover
Directional entrance transitions: slide from bottom, fade from top
Balancing animation speed to keep the experience feeling snappy
lessons.what_learner_does: Adds staggered appear animations to the hero section and service grid.
lessons.why_it_matters: Appear effects introduce content dynamically as visitors scroll through marketing pages.
lessons.expected_outcome: Smooth, staggered appear effects applied to key page sections.

lessons.what_is_taught: Scroll-based interactions in Framer: scroll triggers, scroll-based variant switching, layer movement, sticky positioning on scroll, subtle parallax awareness, and performance considerations.
subtopics: Configuring Scroll Speed and Scroll Transform effects in Framer
Implementing sticky section headers and persistent navigation bars on scroll
Gentle background depth effects without aggressive parallax
Switching component variants based on scroll position milestones
Auditing scroll interaction performance to prevent frame drops
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a sticky navigation header and a scroll-triggered section reveal.
lessons.why_it_matters: Scroll interactions create immersive storytelling when used judiciously.
lessons.expected_outcome: Performant scroll-triggered interactions and sticky navigation.

lessons.what_is_taught: The discipline of animation restraint: preserving text readability, distraction prevention, interaction consistency, mobile motion adaptation, and appropriate animation density.
subtopics: Why excessive parallax and looping 3D effects degrade user experience
Protecting reading comprehension: ensuring text is legible before animating
Simplifying or disabling heavy animations on mobile viewports for battery and speed
Maintaining interaction consistency: unified timing across similar elements
Curating an elegant, restrained aesthetic aligned with modern 2027 design
lessons.what_learner_does: Audits site animations, trims excessive effects, and ensures snappy, restrained motion.
lessons.why_it_matters: Restraint is the hallmark of senior designers; over-animated sites annoy users and hurt conversions.
lessons.expected_outcome: Clean, restrained motion profile that enhances rather than distracts.

lessons.what_is_taught: Accessibility in motion design: keyboard navigation support, focus visibility, meaningful interactive labels, respecting prefers-reduced-motion, avoiding vestibular discomfort, and non-motion alternatives.
subtopics: Understanding vestibular disorders and the importance of reduced motion
How Framer handles prefers-reduced-motion media queries
Ensuring all interactive component states have visible keyboard focus rings
Adding accessible ARIA labels to icon-only buttons and navigation toggles
Providing static visual cues when motion is disabled
lessons.what_learner_does: Tests website with system reduced-motion enabled and verifies accessible focus states.
lessons.why_it_matters: Accessibility ensures all users, including those with disabilities, can navigate comfortably.
lessons.expected_outcome: Accessible motion architecture respecting user reduced-motion preferences.

lessons.what_is_taught: Systematic interaction quality assurance: desktop mouse hover verification, touch screen gesture behavior, keyboard tab access, responsive behavior across screen widths, and 60fps animation performance profiling.
subtopics: Testing hover states across Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Edge
Verifying touch interaction behavior on iOS and Android devices
Testing full keyboard tab navigation through all interactive components
Auditing frame rates during complex scroll transitions using browser DevTools
Documenting interaction specifications for client handoff
lessons.what_learner_does: Conducts systematic cross-platform interaction QA and logs test results.
lessons.why_it_matters: Rigorous interaction QA prevents sticky hover bugs on touch screens and ensures 60fps smoothness.
lessons.expected_outcome: Signed-off interaction QA log demonstrating smooth, bug-free performance.

What is a CMS Collection: tables of structured content items

Understanding dynamic Collection Page Templates

lessons.why_it_matters: A CMS enables clients and marketing teams to add case studies and articles without redesigning pages.

faq.question: What will I learn in this Framer course?
faq.answer: You will learn responsive website design, Framer components, variants, animations, CMS content, SEO settings and publishing workflows through practical website projects.

faq.question: Do I need coding knowledge?
faq.answer: No advanced coding knowledge is required. Basic website design and layout understanding is recommended.

faq.question: Is Figma mandatory?
faq.answer: No. Figma familiarity is useful, but the course also introduces the Framer design workflow and essential design fundamentals.

faq.question: What website will I build?
faq.answer: You will create a multi-page startup, creative agency or portfolio website with reusable components, responsive layouts, interactions and at least one CMS-driven section.

faq.question: Can I use Framer AI?
faq.answer: Yes, where available. You will learn to use supported AI features for initial drafts and ideas, followed by manual design, responsive and accessibility refinement.

faq.question: Does Framer support CMS websites?
faq.answer: Yes. Framer offers CMS capabilities for structured content such as portfolio projects and blog posts. Availability and limits depend on the applicable plan.

faq.question: Will I learn animation and interactions?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn hover effects, component states, scroll interactions and transitions, with attention to usability, performance and accessibility.

faq.question: Is Framer completely free?
faq.answer: Framer provides introductory features, but custom domains and certain advanced capabilities may require paid plans. Students will learn to evaluate these costs.

faq.question: Will I publish a website?
faq.answer: The portfolio includes a published, preview or staged shareable demonstration, depending on the authorized account and applicable platform capabilities.

faq.question: What is the difference between Framer and Webflow?
faq.answer: Framer emphasizes visual design-to-web workflows and interactive marketing experiences. Webflow also provides visual website development, with a strong focus on CSS-oriented layouts, CMS structures and maintainable site architecture. The best choice depends on project needs.

faq.question: Can I use Framer for e-commerce?
faq.answer: This course focuses on marketing websites, portfolios and content sites. Complex transactional e-commerce is outside the course scope.

faq.question: What is the duration and fee?
faq.answer: The course runs for six weeks with 48 guided learning hours. The listed fee is ₹7,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified pricing and tax policy.
